title: What is on top? Stacking and occlusion

sections.skill: Infer stacking order from what is visible

questions.prompt: Rectangular paper sheets are lying flat, one on top of another, seen from directly above. Each sheet is white with a dark outline and a letter in its corner. A sheet hides the parts of the sheets under it. This stack has 3 sheets: A, B, C. Put the sheets in order from the BOTTOM sheet to the TOP sheet.
questions.correct_answer: sheet B → sheet C → sheet A

questions.prompt: Rectangular cards are placed one at a time on an 8 by 8 grid, each covering a block of cells (rows and columns numbered 1 to 8; "rows 1-4, columns 1-4" means a 4 by 4 block). In order: A covers rows 1-4, columns 1-4; B covers rows 3-6, columns 3-6; C covers rows 2-5, columns 2-5; D covers rows 1-3, columns 4-7; E covers rows 5-7, columns 1-3. Seen from above, how many of the five cards can be seen at least partly?

sections.skill: Strategy: the cut-off sheet is underneath
sections.relationship: Students guess the order from size or position. The rule "where two sheets overlap, the one whose outline is cut off is underneath" settles each pair, and the pairs together give the order.
sections.author_note: Students guess the order from size or position. The rule "where two sheets overlap, the one whose outline is cut off is underneath" settles each pair, and the pairs together give the order.

lesson.title: The cut-off sheet is underneath
text: Look at one place where two sheets overlap.
The sheet whose outline runs straight through the overlap is on top there. The sheet whose outline stops at the other sheet's edge is underneath.
Record each pair as "X under Y". Then find the sheet that is under no other sheet: that is the top. Remove it and repeat.
For stacks of centered discs, a disc shows only if every disc above it is smaller.

example.title: Worked example (different sheets)
prompt: Three sheets: the outline of K stops at the edge of M; the outline of M stops at the edge of J; the outline of K stops at the edge of J.
steps: Pairs: K under M, M under J, K under J.
J is under nothing: J is on top.
Then M, then K at the bottom. Order from bottom to top: K, M, J.

questions.prompt: Where sheets X and Y overlap, the outline of X runs straight through and the outline of Y stops at X's edge. What follows?
Pairs found: P under Q, Q under R, P under R. Order the sheets from bottom to top.
questions.correct_answer: sheet P → sheet Q → sheet R

questions.prompt: A sheet whose whole outline can be seen must be on top of every sheet it overlaps.
